### Wrong prompt field name **High Severity** `pm-check-detect.sh` reads `prompt_text` from the `UserPromptSubmit` payload, but Claude Code sends the user text under `prompt`. The extract comes back empty, the hook exits early, and `.pending` is never written, so the PreToolUse gate never denies Write/Edit. The whole pre-build check is a silent no-op in production.
Additional Locations (1) - [`hooks/pm-check-detect.sh#L25-L27`](https://github.com/Traba-Ops/claude-config/blob/6ccecbbe5c549a4932079ed0033723f4cc473380/hooks/pm-check-detect.sh#L25-L27)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 6ccecbbe5c549a4932079ed0033723f4cc473380. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

**[FIX] Claude Opus 5**

Confirmed and fixed in cecd2ad. Verified against [hooks.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md) ("UserPromptSubmit hooks receive the `prompt` field") and against a live Claude Code run — a real UserPromptSubmit payload captured from a session carries `prompt`, no `prompt_text`, and the fixed detector armed `.pending` on it.

The tests were complicit: they fed the hook the same invented field name. New suite at `.github/tests/pm-check-hooks.sh` uses payloads copied from the reference and carries a regression guard asserting a `prompt_text`-only payload does *not* arm the gate.

### Installer aborts on bad hooks **Medium Severity** `event_hooks` still raises `Skip` for a non-list event value, and prune plus PM-hook registration now walk `UserPromptSubmit` and `PreToolUse`. A weird shape on either newly managed event aborts the whole `configure()` pass, so ADHD registration and auto mode never run either. That breaks the install.sh invariant that each settings mutation must degrade independently.
Additional Locations (2) - [`install.sh#L299-L303`](https://github.com/Traba-Ops/claude-config/blob/6ccecbbe5c549a4932079ed0033723f4cc473380/install.sh#L299-L303) - [`install.sh#L247-L258`](https://github.com/Traba-Ops/claude-config/blob/6ccecbbe5c549a4932079ed0033723f4cc473380/install.sh#L247-L258)
 
Triggered by learned rule: install.sh operator safety: file isolation, mutation independence, path parsing Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 6ccecbbe5c549a4932079ed0033723f4cc473380. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

**[FIX] Claude Opus 5**

`event_hooks` no longer raises `Skip`. It returns `None` and records a warning, so a malformed value under one event degrades only that event — ADHD registration, the prune on the other events, and auto mode still land. `Skip` is now reserved for whole-file problems (unreadable, unparseable, un-backup-able).

Also collapsed the three near-identical registration blocks into one `register_hook` helper. Covered by `a malformed hooks.PreToolUse degrades only that event` in the new suite.

[high] Auto-compaction silently lifts the gate
- Why: `SessionStart` fires with `source: "compact"` on **auto or manual compaction**, but this case only exempts `resume | fork`. On `compact` the script falls through and deletes `.pending`, so the gate lifts mid-build — the exact failure the `resume` exemption was written to prevent. `install.sh:275` registers this hook with matcher `startup|resume|clear|compact`, so it will fire. Verified: piping `{"session_id":"SID","source":"compact"}` deletes an existing `.pending`, and `pm-check-gate.sh` then allows the Write. Long build sessions are exactly the ones that auto-compact. Add `compact` to the exempt list.
- Location: `hooks/pm-check-reset.sh:35:3`
- Source: `global-diff`

**[FIX] Claude Opus 5**

Added `compact`. Exempt list is now `resume | fork | compact`.

`clear` deliberately stays non-exempt: `/clear` is an explicit request to start over, so the build request is gone from context and a gate the agent can no longer explain just gets touched away. The next build-shaped prompt re-arms it. Reasoning is in the header comment.

Tests assert marks survive `resume|fork|compact` and are cleared on `startup|clear`.

[high] Prune deletes an operator's own hook when its path does not resolve
- Why: the drop test is `not os.path.exists(script)`, and `os.path.exists` follows symlinks and also returns `False` on a permission error stat'ing a parent. An operator hook living in `~/.claude/hooks/` that is a **symlink into a dotfiles repo, an external drive, or a network mount** is silently deregistered whenever that target is not currently resolvable — `install.sh:47` already acknowledges `hooks/` being "symlinked elsewhere" as a real pattern here. This is newly dangerous because the prune used to be SessionStart-only and now walks `UserPromptSubmit` and `PreToolUse` too. Verified against a temp fixture: a registration for `hooks/my-standup.sh` (broken symlink) was deleted from **both** `UserPromptSubmit` and `PreToolUse`; the same hook as a real file is correctly kept. Consider `os.path.lexists` (keeps broken symlinks) and skipping the prune when the path is unreadable rather than absent.
- Location: `install.sh:329:17`
- Source: `global-diff`

**[FIX] Claude Opus 5**

Replaced with a `definitely_absent()` helper: `os.lstat`, `FileNotFoundError` → prune, any other `OSError` → keep. So a broken symlink, an offline mount, and an untraversable parent all read as "still there".

Tests cover all three outcomes — a hook symlinked at an unresolvable target is kept, a real file is kept, a genuinely absent script is dropped.

[medium] Verb alternation has no leading word boundary, so edits to existing things get gated
- Why: the noun group uses `\b(...)\b` but the verb group does not, so any word *ending* in a listed verb matches. Verified on macOS BSD grep — these all trip the gate: `rebuild the report`, `readd the endpoint`, `unmake the pipeline`. That directly contradicts `skills/pm-check/SKILL.md:22-23` ("Do not run it for edits to something that already exists, bug fixes, refactors") — "rebuild the report" is the canonical edit case. Also `add a test to the job runner` gates, though the PR description claims requiring both keeps `write a test` from tripping it: the noun `job` catches it. Suggest `\b(build|create|add|...)\b`.
- Location: `hooks/pm-check-detect.sh:43:1`
- Source: `global-diff`

**[FIX] Claude Opus 5**

Now `\b(build|create|add|implement|make|set up|setup|spin up|write)\b`. Your three cases are in the suite as explicit non-matches, alongside a positive case for the multi-word `set up` so the boundary change did not break it.

[medium] The completion `touch` cannot be run as written
- Why: an agent has no way to resolve `<session_id>` — the session id is not exposed to it as a variable or environment value. Verified: running the snippet literally creates a file named `claude-pm-check-<session_id>.done`, which does not lift the gate, and the session stays blocked with no obvious recovery. The fallback at line 107 ("the blocked-tool message contains the exact path") does not cover the common path either: in the normal flow the detector's `additionalContext` invokes this skill *before* any Write is attempted, so there is no blocked-tool message yet. The good news is the detector's injected context does carry the full absolute path — line 107 should point at that message too, and the code block should not show a placeholder that fails silently when copied.
- Location: `skills/pm-check/SKILL.md:104:1`
- Source: `global-diff`

**[FIX] Claude Opus 5**

You were right that the placeholder is unresolvable, and right that the line-107 fallback does not cover the normal flow. Fixed with a real mechanism rather than better prose.

`CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` is a SessionStart-only facility ([hooks.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md#persist-environment-variables)): exports appended there are picked up by every subsequent Bash tool call. `pm-check-reset.sh` is already a SessionStart hook and already has the `session_id`, so it now writes:

```sh
export CLAUDE_PM_CHECK_DONE='<TMPDIR>/claude-pm-check-<session_id>.done'
```

written *before* the source-based early exit, so resumed, forked, and compacted sessions get it too. SKILL.md step 6 is now `touch "$CLAUDE_PM_CHECK_DONE"` with an explicit "do not reconstruct this yourself" note, and the fallback (hooks installed mid-session, so SessionStart has not run) points at both messages that carry the literal path.

Verified end to end in the suite: reset → detect → gate denies → source the env file and run the exact SKILL.md command → gate allows.

[medium] Subagent writes are gated under the parent's session id
- Why: extraction reads only `session_id`. Per the hooks reference, `PreToolUse` fires inside subagents and the payload carries `agent_id`/`agent_type` as the documented discriminator, while `session_id` stays the parent's. Verified: a payload with `session_id: PSID` plus `agent_id: sub-1` is denied off the parent's `.pending`. So delegating implementation to a subagent produces a denial inside an agent that never saw the detector's context and cannot invoke the skill meaningfully — it can only `touch` its way out, which trains exactly the bypass reflex this is meant to prevent. Worth deciding explicitly: either exempt subagents (`agent_id` present) or make the deny message subagent-aware.
- Location: `hooks/pm-check-gate.sh:27:1`
- Source: `global-diff`

left by /bugbot-code-review skill

Is this useful
- [ ] Yes
- [ ] No (a comment is helpful but not necessary)

**[FIX] Claude Opus 5**

Exempting subagents. `agent_id` is present only inside a subagent call, so the gate now exits early when it is set.

Reasoning: denying there is strictly worse than allowing. The subagent never saw the detector's context, cannot run the check meaningfully, and its only exit is `touch` — which is the same bypass with more confusion, and it teaches the reflex the gate exists to prevent. The parent stays gated for its own writes, and the parent is where the decision to build is made. A parent that spawns a subagent purely to route around the gate has done something more deliberate than the documented `~/.claude/.pm-check-off` opt-out, which is a guardrail's job to allow.

Documented in the hook comment and in SKILL.md, alongside the `Bash` hole for the same reason (the skill needs Bash to record completion).

[medium] Bundle spec and README not updated for a write-blocking feature
- Why: `docs/skill-bundle-spec.md:39` states the rule directly — "anything that needs installer-side setup (a flag file, a `settings.json` hook registration) stays inert on existing installs until the operator re-runs the curl installer. **Ship setup-dependent features with a note telling existing operators to re-run it.**" This PR is exactly that case and ships no such note, so every existing operator gets `skills/pm-check/` via the hourly `git pull` while the three hooks stay unregistered. Separately, the spec's feature table (lines 15-27) and `README.md` both document ADHD mode in detail but gain no entry for a hook that **denies Write/Edit org-wide** — the first operator it blocks has nothing to read.
- Location: `skills/pm-check/SKILL.md:1:1`
- Source: `global-diff`

**[FIX] Claude Opus 5**

All three added:

- `docs/skill-bundle-spec.md` — a full "Pre-build PM check (on by default)" section with a blockquoted re-run-the-installer note, matching the rule at line 39.
- Bundle-spec feature table — a row for the skill plus the three hooks.
- `README.md` — a "What You Get" entry in operator language, including what to do when Claude says it is blocked and the `.pm-check-off` escape hatch. Also rewrote the "Already installed?" callout to lead with **re-run the curl command** and name this feature.

[low] Sweep window is 48h, not "older than a day", and can unlock a live session
- Why: `-mtime +1` means strictly more than one 24h period, so it matches at 48h. Verified on BSD find: a 30h-old flag is **not** swept, a 50h-old one is — the comment above says "older than a day". Second-order effect worth a thought: the sweep is unconditional, so a genuinely long-lived session whose `.pending` is 48h+ old has its gate lifted by any *other* session starting up. Neither is severe, but the comment should match the behaviour.
- Location: `hooks/pm-check-reset.sh:30:1`
- Source: `global-diff`

**[FIX] Claude Opus 5**

Comment fixed to state 48h and why. Kept `-mtime +1` rather than shortening it: the sweep is unconditional, so a shorter window is *likelier* to hit your second-order case and lift a live session's gate, and cleanup latency does not matter here. That tradeoff is now in the comment.

- Why: `Write|Edit|MultiEdit` leaves `NotebookEdit` ungated, so a build that lands in a notebook skips the check entirely. Cheap to add. [low] nit: comment says "first match"; the regex takes the last
- Why: the leading `.*` is greedy, so `sed` anchors on the *final* occurrence of the field. Verified: `{"session_id":"FIRST","other":1,"session_id":"LAST"}` yields `LAST`. Harmless for today's payloads (and prompt-borne injection is blocked, since a `"` inside the prompt arrives escaped as `\"` and breaks the match), but the comment states the opposite of the behaviour, which is the kind of thing someone later relies on.
- Location: `hooks/pm-check-detect.sh:27:1`
- Source: `global-diff`
